title: The Mustang's first flight
photoNote: The NA-73X prototype, civil registration NX19998, in 1940. North American Aviation photo, public domain on Wikimedia Commons. Small original (894 px).
body:
In 1940 Britain was fighting for its life and needed fighters fast. It asked an American company to build someone else's design. The company offered to build a better one.

26 October 1940. Test pilot Vance Breese took the prototype, the NA-73X, into the air for the first time at Mines Field in Los Angeles. It had gone from order to rollout in less than four months.

Britain had already ordered 320 and called it the Mustang. Its Allison engine lost power up high, so the RAF flew the first Mustangs low, on reconnaissance and ground attack.

Fitted later with the Rolls-Royce Merlin, the Mustang could escort bombers from England deep into Germany and back. More than 15,000 were built.

Which fighter of the war would you most like to see fly?

#OnThisDay #WW2
